title: Vanessa Van Edwards: The Conversation Habit That Makes Smart People Unlikable (Part 1)

lines.en: How do you know you talk too much?
lines.zh: 你怎麼知道自己話太多？

lines.en: So, first thing is non-verbal cues.
lines.zh: 首先是非語言的線索。

lines.en: Someone is checking out if they are opening their mouth as if to say something.
lines.zh: 看對方是不是張開嘴、好像想說什麼。

lines.en: I call it like the open fish.
lines.zh: 我把它叫做「張嘴的魚」。

lines.en: And that's a subtle cue that you talk too much.
lines.zh: 那是一個很細微的線索，代表你話太多了。

lines.en: Do you think they're listening right now and think that's me? Yes.
lines.zh: 你覺得他們現在在聽的時候，會不會想說「那就是我」？會。

lines.en: And there was a recent study where they found that 95% of people have worked with someone who talks too much.
lines.zh: 最近有一項研究發現，95% 的人都曾經和話太多的人共事過。

lines.en: Well, I have a do you talk too much test?
lines.zh: 我有一個「你是不是話太多」的測驗。

lines.en: So, there's five questions here and if you answer more than three times, you're probably an overtalker. Yeah.
lines.zh: 這裡有五個問題，如果你超過三題回答是，你大概就是個話太多的人。對。

lines.en: Cuz my next question is like which one's worse, over talking or undertalking?
lines.zh: 因為我下一個問題是，哪一個比較糟，話太多還是話太少？

lines.en: Well, I have spent the last 20 years studying master conversationalists and I found that it's the vehicle to get what you want and I'm a recovering awkward person and I really struggled with bad conversation for a long time.
lines.zh: 我花了過去 20 年研究對話高手，我發現對話是得到你想要的東西的工具，而我是一個正在康復中的尷尬人，很長一段時間都很苦於不會聊天。

lines.en: But I think the next generations will be talking to technology more than they talk to humans.
lines.zh: 但我覺得下一代跟科技說話的時間，會比跟人說話還多。

lines.en: And because we're having less conversations, one in six people worldwide are affected by loneliness.
lines.zh: 而因為我們的對話越來越少，全世界每六個人就有一個受到孤獨影響。

lines.en: And I now more than ever am sending 9-minute voice notes to my friends.
lines.zh: 而我現在比以往任何時候都更常傳 9 分鐘的語音訊息給朋友。

lines.en: But a voice note, it's the most selfish form of conversation. that in this age of technological change, the people who are masterful at conversation are going to have an advantage.
lines.zh: 但語音訊息是最自私的一種對話形式。在這個科技變遷的時代，擅長對話的人將會有優勢。

lines.en: But there's a blueprint to good conversation.
lines.zh: 但好的對話是有藍圖的。

lines.en: And once you know the blueprint, it becomes easier.
lines.zh: 一旦你知道了藍圖，對話就會變簡單。

lines.en: For example, we devised three different speed networking experiments with 500 speed networkers.
lines.zh: 例如，我們設計了三個不同的快速社交實驗，找了 500 位快速社交的參與者。

lines.en: And the best conversation starter was actually what was the highlight of your day?
lines.zh: 而最好的開場白其實是：你今天最棒的事是什麼？

lines.en: Because the moment we asked how are you, what do you do?
lines.zh: 因為我們一問「你好嗎？你是做什麼的？」

lines.en: They ran out of things to talk about.
lines.zh: 他們就沒話題可聊了。

lines.en: But the worst question in the history of conversations is but I also have a formula to immediately bypass that small talk.
lines.zh: 但史上最糟的對話問題是……但我也有一個公式，可以立刻跳過那些閒聊。

lines.en: Also a secret door to charisma but also there are five archetypes and this is going to impact getting our promotion and finding your soulmate.
lines.zh: 還有通往魅力的秘密之門，還有五種原型，這會影響你能不能升遷、能不能找到靈魂伴侶。

lines.en: We're going to go through all of them but one of the ways to get out of a bad conversation without offending people.
lines.zh: 我們會一一談到，還有其中一種不冒犯人、又能脫離糟糕對話的方法。

lines.en: Well, we tend to focus a lot on the first impression, but we don't really think about the end.
lines.zh: 我們往往很重視第一印象，但我們不太會去想結尾。

lines.en: But it's all really important and I discovered this framework. So
lines.zh: 但這些都非常重要，而我發現了這個架構。所以

lines.en: Vanessa Van Edwards, on page five of your new book, Conversations, you talk about how we're in a connection crisis, and you say that conversations are getting harder, more awkward, and less satisfying.
lines.zh: 呃，Vanessa Van Edwards，你的新書《Conversations》第五頁提到，我們正處於一場連結危機，你說對話變得越來越難、越來越尷尬、越來越不令人滿足。

lines.en: At some level, I feel that too.
lines.zh: 某種程度上我也有這種感覺。

lines.en: My question to you is, why did you choose to write this book based on, you know, everything you could have written about, everything we've talked about before?
lines.zh: 我的問題是，在所有你能寫的主題、所有我們之前談過的東西之中，你為什麼選擇寫這本書？

lines.en: Why is this book needed at this time?
lines.zh: 為什麼現在需要這本書？

lines.en: People who are investing in conversation skills right now are creating career insurance.
lines.zh: 現在投資在對話技巧上的人，是在為自己的職涯買保險。

lines.en: We like to work with people who are great at conversation.
lines.zh: 我們喜歡和很會聊天的人共事。

lines.en: We like to be with people who are great at conversation.
lines.zh: 我們喜歡和很會聊天的人在一起。

lines.en: We like to date people who are good at conversation.
lines.zh: 我們喜歡和很會聊天的人約會。

lines.en: And in this age of tremendous technological change, the people who are masterful at conversation are going to have an advantage.
lines.zh: 而在這個科技劇烈變遷的時代，擅長對話的人將會有優勢。

lines.en: So, I wrote this right now because we are slowly losing our ability to connect.
lines.zh: 所以我現在寫這本書，是因為我們正在慢慢失去與人連結的能力。

lines.en: And I think this is the last generation that will learn about conversation via human.
lines.zh: 而我覺得這是最後一個透過人類學習對話的世代。

lines.en: I think the next generations will be talking to technology more than they talk to humans.
lines.zh: 我覺得下一代跟科技說話的時間，會比跟人說話還多。

lines.en: Is it possible to be great at conversation?
lines.zh: 有可能變得很會聊天嗎？

lines.en: And if I become great at conversation through what we're about to talk about today, what is the advantage that you're speaking about there?
lines.zh: 如果我透過今天要談的內容變得很會聊天，你說的優勢是什麼？

lines.en: What advantage will I experience in my life?
lines.zh: 我的人生會得到什麼優勢？

lines.en: For everybody listening now, what advantage will they see in their life relative to where they are now?
lines.zh: 對每一個現在正在聽的人來說，相較於他們現在的狀況，他們的人生會看到什麼優勢？

lines.en: Conversation is the vehicle to get what you want, right?
lines.zh: 對話是得到你想要的東西的工具，對吧？

lines.en: If you want a promotion and you can chat with your boss where they connect with you, you're more likely to be thought of for that promotion.
lines.zh: 如果你想升遷，而你能和老闆聊得讓他跟你產生連結，你就更有可能被列入升遷的考慮。

lines.en: If you want to meet your soulmate, you have to have deep, connected, meaningful conversation to truly get to know each other.
lines.zh: 如果你想遇見靈魂伴侶，你們必須有深入、有連結、有意義的對話，才能真正了解彼此。

lines.en: If you are lonely, finding friends that are actually fulfilling and give you the joy of conversation is going to give you a longevity boost.
lines.zh: 如果你很孤單，找到真正讓你感到充實、給你對話樂趣的朋友，會讓你更長壽。

lines.en: I think that the mistake that we have made is we think of conversation as extra.
lines.zh: 我覺得我們犯的錯，是把對話當成額外的東西。

lines.en: You know, we sort of put it second.
lines.zh: 你知道，我們有點把它擺在第二位。

lines.en: I know leaders focus on this a lot where they're focused so much on their idea, on their technology, on their business, but they forget about the human element.
lines.zh: 我知道很多領導者都有這個問題，他們太專注在自己的點子、技術、生意上，卻忘了人的因素。

lines.en: And I think we have to start thinking about conversation almost like going to the gym.
lines.zh: 我覺得我們得開始把對話想成像上健身房一樣。

lines.en: You know, we we focused a lot on our physical health, but our social health is critical to our emotional health, right?
lines.zh: 你知道，我們很重視身體健康，但我們的社交健康對情緒健康至關重要，對吧？

lines.en: If we are doing conversation reps, if we can truly become good at conversation and conversation, I think is a skill to learn.
lines.zh: 如果我們持續練習對話，如果我們真的能變得很會聊天，我覺得對話是一種可以學會的技能。

lines.en: I don't think it you're born with it or you're not.
lines.zh: 我不覺得那是天生的，有就有、沒有就沒有。

lines.en: I think you can learn to be good at conversation.
lines.zh: 我覺得你可以學會變得很會聊天。

lines.en: And it's the one skill that keeps on giving.
lines.zh: 而且這是一項會一直帶來回報的技能。

lines.en: Do people tend to know if they're good or bad at conversation?
lines.zh: 大家通常知道自己很會聊天還是不會聊天嗎？

lines.en: Like are there symptoms one experiences when they when they're not good at conversation?
lines.zh: 不會聊天的人會有什麼症狀嗎？

lines.en: Are they aware of that?
lines.zh: 他們自己有意識到嗎？

lines.en: Yes, there is symptoms of being a bad conversationalist.
lines.zh: 有，不會聊天是有症狀的。

lines.en: And by the way, I should back up.
lines.zh: 順帶一提，我應該先倒回去講一下。

lines.en: As you know, I'm a recovering awkward person and I really struggled with bad conversation for a long time.
lines.zh: 你知道，我是一個正在康復中的尷尬人，很長一段時間都很苦於不會聊天。

lines.en: And I realized it was because I was asking the wrong questions and I was approaching conversation the wrong way.
lines.zh: 我後來發現，那是因為我問錯了問題，用錯誤的方式在面對對話。

lines.en: And the wrong way to approach conversation is trying to impress, not discover.
lines.zh: 而面對對話的錯誤方式，是試圖讓人印象深刻，而不是去探索。

lines.en: If you're trying to impress people, conversation becomes performative.
lines.zh: 如果你試圖讓人印象深刻，對話就會變成一場表演。

lines.en: And that is so deeply unfulfilling. Right?
lines.zh: 而那讓人非常沒有滿足感，對吧？

lines.en: That is when small talk becomes soul crushing.
lines.zh: 這時候閒聊就會變得讓人心力交瘁。

lines.en: I have spent the last 20 years studying master conversationalists.
lines.zh: 我花了過去 20 年研究對話高手。

lines.en: Master conversationalists, they live differently in the world, and I only know this cuz I wasn't one for a long time.
lines.zh: 對話高手在這個世界上的生活方式不一樣，我會知道，是因為我很長一段時間都不是。

lines.en: They are not only more joyous, but they're also more confident. They're more authentically assertive.
lines.zh: 他們不只更快樂，也更有自信。他們更能真誠地堅定表達自己。

lines.en: They get more energy from interactions, whether they're an introvert or extrovert, because their conversations are giving them energy, not taking energy.
lines.zh: 他們從互動中得到更多能量，不管是內向還是外向，因為他們的對話給他們能量，而不是消耗能量。

lines.en: The symptom of bad conversation and I I hate to give someone a label of being a bad conversationalist, an exhausted conversationalist is you dread it.
lines.zh: 不會聊天的症狀，我很不喜歡給人貼上「不會聊天」的標籤，一個對對話感到筋疲力盡的人，會很怕對話。

lines.en: Dread is a really important emotion.
lines.zh: 「害怕」是一種非常重要的情緒。

lines.en: If you open your calendar and you see only dread or you feel only dread, there's something wrong, right?
lines.zh: 如果你打開行事曆，只看到害怕、只感到害怕，那就是哪裡出了問題，對吧？

lines.en: Conversation like boosts us, gives us energy.
lines.zh: 對話應該能提振我們、給我們能量。

lines.en: So you feel dread in social interactions.
lines.zh: 所以你在社交互動中會感到害怕。

lines.en: Um you feel overwhelmed when you're in conversation.
lines.zh: 嗯，你在對話中會感到不知所措。

lines.en: So if you're in conversation and you're social overthinking, you cannot turn your brain off.
lines.zh: 如果你在對話中社交過度思考，你沒辦法讓大腦停下來。

lines.en: All you're worried about is what you're going to say next.
lines.zh: 你只擔心自己接下來要說什麼。

lines.en: It's actually just because you probably haven't learned the mechanics of conversation blue.
lines.zh: 其實這只是因為你可能還沒學會對話的運作方式。

lines.en: There's a blueprint to good conversation.
lines.zh: 好的對話是有藍圖的。

lines.en: We're going to talk about it.
lines.zh: 我們會談到它。

lines.en: Once you know the blueprint, it becomes easier.
lines.zh: 一旦你知道了藍圖，對話就會變簡單。

lines.en: And the last symptom of bad conversation is that you leave feeling misunderstood.
lines.zh: 不會聊天的最後一個症狀，是你離開時覺得被誤解了。

lines.en: You leave feeling like I was the worst version of myself or I wasn't able to be my best self.
lines.zh: 你離開時覺得：我展現了最糟的自己，或是我沒辦法做最好的自己。

lines.en: I think really good conversationalist people leave conversation with them thinking, wow, I after talking to you, I feel like I understand myself better.
lines.zh: 我覺得真正很會聊天的人，會讓和他們聊過的人離開時心想：哇，跟你聊完之後，我覺得我更了解我自己了。

lines.en: And that's a very different way of thinking about oh I want to impress somebody.
lines.zh: 這和「喔，我想讓別人印象深刻」是非常不同的思考方式。

lines.en: So how long have you spent doing the research that feeds into what we're going to talk about today and feeds into this new book. Okay.
lines.zh: 那你花了多久時間做研究，支撐今天要談的內容、支撐這本新書？好。

lines.en: So accidentally I've been doing research for this my whole life because I was very bad at conversation for 20 years.
lines.zh: 所以我其實不小心一輩子都在做這項研究，因為我有 20 年都非常不會聊天。

lines.en: Then 20 years ago I realized that there are these hidden blueprints behind our interactions.
lines.zh: 然後 20 年前，我發現我們的互動背後有一些隱藏的藍圖。

lines.en: I wasn't quite sure what they were but I could see that very good conversationalists they were following some kind of plan.
lines.zh: 我不太確定那是什麼，但我看得出來，很會聊天的人都遵循著某種計畫。

lines.en: Then eight years ago, this is when the real research began.
lines.zh: 然後八年前，真正的研究開始了。

lines.en: And it started with an experiment.
lines.zh: 一開始是一個實驗。

lines.en: I call it my speed networking experiment.
lines.zh: 我把它叫做快速社交實驗。

lines.en: This fundamentally changed the way I think about conversations.
lines.zh: 它從根本上改變了我對對話的看法。

lines.en: So here's what we did.
lines.zh: 我們是這樣做的。

lines.en: I knew there was some secret the conversationalists had and I was like, I'm going to find it.
lines.zh: 我知道對話高手有某種秘密，我想：我一定要找出來。

lines.en: So we devised three different speed networking experiments with 500 speed networkers.
lines.zh: 所以我們設計了三個不同的快速社交實驗，找了 500 位快速社交的參與者。

lines.en: We brought them in these rooms and we had cameras set up in all four corners of the room because good conversation looks different. Really good conversation.
lines.zh: 我們把他們帶進房間，在房間四個角落都架了攝影機，因為好的對話看起來就不一樣。真正好的對話。

lines.en: You've seen you do you ever like you know show a lot
lines.zh: 你看過……你有沒有……

lines.en: of restroom like are they having a bad day?
lines.zh: ……像是他們今天很不順嗎？

lines.en: Um, so you know a good conversation is a lot of gestures, a lot of leaning.
lines.zh: 嗯，你知道，好的對話會有很多手勢、很多身體前傾。

lines.en: It, you know, has that high energy.
lines.zh: 它有那種高能量。

lines.en: You see a lot of vocal charisma. The volume goes up.
lines.zh: 你會看到很多聲音上的魅力，音量會提高。

lines.en: In a bad conversation, it sort of sounds like this.
lines.zh: 而糟糕的對話聽起來有點像這樣。

lines.en: Like it has like very low energy, like apologetic facial expressions, like low volume.
lines.zh: 能量很低，表情像在道歉，音量很小。

lines.en: Then I assigned these networkers six conversation starters.
lines.zh: 然後我給這些參與者六個開場白。

lines.en: Now, I picked these conversation starters.
lines.zh: 這些開場白是我挑的。

lines.en: I'm going to tell you what they are very carefully.
lines.zh: 我會很仔細地告訴你是哪些。

lines.en: Three of them I thought could do really well and three of them I wasn't sure about. I wanted to see.
lines.zh: 其中三個我覺得效果會很好，另外三個我不確定。我想看看結果。

lines.en: We gave them these six conversation starters and we asked them after each timed conversation to rate the quality of it.
lines.zh: 我們給他們這六個開場白，在每一場限時對話後請他們替對話品質打分數。

lines.en: One being that was the worst most awkward conversation I've ever had to five being that was the best conversation I ever had.
lines.zh: 1 分是我這輩子最糟、最尷尬的對話，5 分是我這輩子最好的對話。

lines.en: I want to marry this person or I want to connect with them on LinkedIn.
lines.zh: 我想跟這個人結婚，或我想在 LinkedIn 上加他好友。

lines.en: Then we took all these ratings and we ranked them and there were clear winners and clear losers.
lines.zh: 然後我們把所有分數排名，有明顯的贏家和明顯的輸家。

lines.en: The losers, the conversations that produced the worst connection, the most awkwardness were last choice.
lines.zh: 輸家，也就是產生最差連結、最尷尬的對話，是最後一名。

lines.en: Want to guess what last choice was? Last
lines.zh: 想猜猜最後一名是什麼嗎？最後

lines.en: in terms of an opener
lines.zh: 以開場白來說，

lines.en: in in terms of just a question.
lines.zh: 以單純的問題來說。

lines.en: A typical question you ask my first minutes.
lines.zh: 你在頭幾分鐘會問的典型問題。

lines.en: Number five, that was the fifth worst.
lines.zh: 第五名，那是倒數第二差的。

lines.en: Very close to the bottom. Sixth was something about the weather.
lines.zh: 非常接近墊底。第六名是跟天氣有關的。

lines.en: That what do you do? What do you do? That was the worst. The worst. Okay. Why?
lines.zh: 「你是做什麼的？」你是做什麼的？那是最差的。最差的。好。為什麼？

lines.en: So these last two, how are you and what do you do?
lines.zh: 所以最後這兩個，「你好嗎」和「你是做什麼的」。

lines.en: They're very socially scripted, right?
lines.zh: 它們是非常制式化的社交劇本，對吧？

lines.en: The moment we ask those questions, our brain goes into autopilot.
lines.zh: 我們一問出這些問題，大腦就會進入自動駕駛模式。

lines.en: So, uh there's a lack there a is more of a performance.
lines.zh: 所以，呃，比較像是一場表演。

lines.en: There's a lack of like excitement in the conversation and they ran out of things to talk about.
lines.zh: 對話裡缺乏興奮感，他們也沒話題可聊了。

lines.en: They're fact-based questions and this is the trap of what we'll call level one conversation which is you are trapped in fact. Where are you from?
lines.zh: 這些是事實型問題，這就是我們所說的第一層對話的陷阱：你被困在事實裡。你從哪裡來？

lines.en: Got any kids? Married? The facts are dead ends, right?
lines.zh: 有小孩嗎？結婚了嗎？事實是死胡同，對吧？

lines.en: So, they're there it's very hard for someone to break out of that fact because they're stuck in that social that social script.
lines.zh: 所以對方很難跳脫那個事實，因為他們被困在那個社交劇本裡。

lines.en: The best conversation starter was actually a sneaker.
lines.zh: 最好的開場白其實是一匹黑馬。

lines.en: I was like, interesting that this one did best by lot.
lines.zh: 我想：有意思，這個竟然大勝。

lines.en: It was, "What was the highlight of your day?"
lines.zh: 那就是：「你今天最棒的事是什麼？」

lines.en: Now, what this question does psychologically, it sounds casual.
lines.zh: 這個問題在心理上的作用是，它聽起來很隨意。

lines.en: Well, first of all, it's not too deep.
lines.zh: 首先，它不會太深入。

lines.en: A mistake that extroverts can make is they ask too deep too question too quickly, right?
lines.zh: 外向的人常犯的錯，是太快問太深入的問題，對吧？

lines.en: They they're like, "What is your greatest goal in life?"
lines.zh: 他們會問：「你人生最大的目標是什麼？」

lines.en: And you're like, "I don't know you." Right?
lines.zh: 你就想：「我又不認識你。」對吧？

lines.en: So, it's not too deep, but it's a subtle replacement for how are you?
lines.zh: 所以它不會太深入，但它巧妙地取代了「你好嗎？」

lines.en: You're actually asking the other person's brain to search for optimism.
lines.zh: 你其實是在請對方的大腦去搜尋樂觀的東西。

lines.en: You're literally inviting their brain to think like what was good and then they think well highlight of my day.
lines.zh: 你是在邀請對方的大腦去想什麼是好的，然後他們會想：嗯，我今天最棒的事。

lines.en: So one we just broke autopilot.
lines.zh: 所以第一，我們打破了自動駕駛模式。

lines.en: The most the moment someone goes oh and they're thinking for the first time their brain goes oo we get to we get to do something new.
lines.zh: 當有人說「喔」、第一次開始思考的那一刻，他們的大腦會想：喔，我們可以做點新的事了。

lines.en: So they got to think of something new and it was immediate like it wasn't like a too big of a question.
lines.zh: 所以他們得想點新的東西，而且可以立刻回答，不是一個太大的問題。

lines.en: The second question was have anything exciting you're working on.
lines.zh: 第二個問題是：「最近有在忙什麼令人興奮的事嗎？」

lines.en: This is kind of a subtle replacement for what do you do? Right? Right?
lines.zh: 這有點像是巧妙地取代「你是做什麼的？」對吧？對吧？

lines.en: If someone likes what they do, they're going to talk about it, but they're going to reframe it in something exciting.
lines.zh: 如果有人喜歡自己的工作，他們會聊工作，但會把它換成令人興奮的角度。

lines.en: And if someone someone isn't defined by what they do, they're going to share something better.
lines.zh: 如果有人不是用工作來定義自己，他們會分享更好的東西。

lines.en: The third question, very, very simple, was do you have any fun plans coming up?
lines.zh: 第三個問題非常非常簡單：「最近有什麼好玩的計畫嗎？」

lines.en: These questions, the three first three are literally searching for good.
lines.zh: 這三個問題，前三個，都是在搜尋好的東西。

lines.en: You're inviting other person to only think about good things and we're juicing excitement for other parts of their life.
lines.zh: 你在邀請對方只去想好的事，也在為他們生活中的其他部分注入興奮感。

lines.en: Now, the fourth question, the middle one, almost broke my data.
lines.zh: 而第四個問題，中間那個，差點把我的數據搞壞。

lines.en: And this is where things really got interesting for me as a researcher.
lines.zh: 這也是作為研究者，我覺得最有意思的地方。

lines.en: This fourth question, people either loved it or they hated it.
lines.zh: 這第四個問題，大家不是超愛就是超討厭。

lines.en: They either gave it a five, that was like the most connective thing I felt all week, or a zero.
lines.zh: 他們不是給 5 分，覺得那是整個禮拜最有連結感的事，就是給 0 分。

lines.en: And a zero wasn't even an option on my scale.
lines.zh: 而 0 分根本不在我的量表上。

lines.en: It was the question, what's your story? Now, what's your story?
lines.zh: 那個問題是：「說說你的故事吧？」「說說你的故事」。

lines.en: Have you ever been asked that question, by the way? Derivatives of that question. Okay.
lines.zh: 順帶一提，你有被問過這個問題嗎？或類似的問題？好。

lines.en: So extroverts tend to default to that question because they want to go a little bit deeper.
lines.zh: 外向的人往往會預設問這個問題，因為他們想聊得深入一點。

lines.en: But actually that is a level three question.
lines.zh: 但其實那是一個第三層的問題。

lines.en: It is way too advanced for someone who's introverted or someone who has never like framed their story that quickly.
lines.zh: 對內向的人，或是從來沒有那麼快整理過自己故事的人來說，這太進階了。

lines.en: They're immediately put into cortisol.
lines.zh: 他們會立刻分泌皮質醇。

lines.en: They're immediately put into fight or flight.
lines.zh: 他們會立刻進入戰或逃的模式。

lines.en: They're like what's my story?
lines.zh: 他們會想：我的故事是什麼？

lines.en: Like how can I give that to you so quickly?
lines.zh: 我怎麼能這麼快就講給你聽？

lines.en: So you're by accident putting them into conversational fear.
lines.zh: 所以你不小心讓他們陷入了對話恐懼。

lines.en: This is when I realize there's a hierarchy.
lines.zh: 那時我才明白，對話是有層級的。

lines.en: We have to move through our conversations with different levels, right?
lines.zh: 我們在對話中必須逐步經過不同的層級，對吧？

lines.en: This is why we have this.
lines.zh: 這就是我們有這個的原因。

lines.en: So for anyone that can't see because you're listening on Apple Music or Spotify or whatever, we have a three tier little stage in front of us.
lines.zh: 對於看不到畫面、在 Apple Music 或 Spotify 之類平台收聽的人，我們面前有一個三層的小台階。

lines.en: Tier one, tier two, tier three.
lines.zh: 第一層、第二層、第三層。

lines.en: What are these three tiers? Okay, so Dr.
lines.zh: 這三層是什麼？好，Dr.

lines.en: Dan McAdams found that conversation is actually not as fluid as we would like to think. that actually when we're trying to connect with someone else, we are trying to move through three distinct levels.
lines.zh: Dan McAdams 發現，對話其實沒有我們以為的那麼流動。其實當我們試著和別人建立連結時，我們是在經過三個不同的層級。

lines.en: Level one is called general traits.
lines.zh: 第一層叫做「一般特質」。

lines.en: This is why in those first few minutes you're basically trying to Google fact check someone like where are you from? What do you do? Married?
lines.zh: 這就是為什麼在頭幾分鐘，你基本上是在 Google 查證一個人，像是你從哪裡來？你做什麼的？結婚了嗎？

lines.en: Where do you live in LA? Right?
lines.zh: 你住在洛杉磯哪裡？對吧？

lines.en: Like you're trying to ask all those questions because there's a sort of social hierarchy.
lines.zh: 你會問這些問題，是因為有一種社交上的層級順序。

lines.en: Our brain processes social facts from least least intimate to most intimate.
lines.zh: 我們的大腦處理社交資訊，是從最不私密到最私密。

lines.en: So we cannot get to know someone on their deepest dreams and worries if we don't know the basic facts about them.
lines.zh: 所以如果我們不知道一個人的基本資訊，就沒辦法認識他最深的夢想和煩惱。

lines.en: So that is why we often fall into that trap of those fact-based questions.
lines.zh: 這就是為什麼我們常常掉進那些事實型問題的陷阱。

lines.en: The key here is that really good level one question is taking those facts but adding story but adding emotion.
lines.zh: 這裡的關鍵是，真正好的第一層問題，是把那些事實加上故事、加上情緒。

lines.en: So the the best way to to do level one better is you're swapping out those bad questions, right? How are you?
lines.zh: 所以把第一層做得更好的最佳方法，是把那些糟糕的問題換掉，對吧？「你好嗎？」

lines.en: What do you do with looking for a story?
lines.zh: 「你是做什麼的？」換成尋找故事的問題。

lines.en: I truly believe a fact is a is a stop sign.
lines.zh: 我真心相信，事實是一個停止標誌。

lines.en: A story is a doorway.
lines.zh: 故事是一扇門。

lines.en: Give me an example of both. Okay.
lines.zh: 兩個都舉個例子給我聽。好。

lines.en: So, um one of them we're actually we can place it on here is what's your personal passion project? Okay.
lines.zh: 嗯，其中一個，我們可以把它放在這裡，就是：「你個人熱衷的專案是什麼？」好。

lines.en: Now, what's your personal passion project is actually a hunt for stories, right?
lines.zh: 「你個人熱衷的專案是什麼？」其實是在尋找故事，對吧？

lines.en: And would you open with that?
lines.zh: 你會用這句當開場嗎？

lines.en: Is that what you're saying?
lines.zh: 你是這個意思嗎？

lines.en: Or is it doesn't really matter?
lines.zh: 還是其實沒關係？

lines.en: It has to come it can come in the first few minutes.
lines.zh: 它必須……它可以在頭幾分鐘出現。

lines.en: Now, I probably wouldn't walk into a room and be like, "What's your personal passion project, Stephen?" Right?
lines.zh: 我大概不會一走進房間就說：「Stephen，你個人熱衷的專案是什麼？」對吧？

lines.en: It's it's a little bit much.
lines.zh: 那有點太過了。

lines.en: We have to do our basic first impression and we can talk about you know first 10 words in a little bit but as an opener question it's better than how are you
lines.zh: 我們得先建立基本的第一印象，等一下可以談談開頭的 10 個字，但作為開場問題，它比「你好嗎」好。

lines.en: and I have to pause here and say everything I'm going to share takes a little bit of conversational courage
lines.zh: 我得在這裡停一下說，我要分享的每一件事，都需要一點對話上的勇氣。

lines.en: it's really safe to ask how are you really safe to ask what do you do but if you want to be memorable if you want to actually spark connection those won't serve you
lines.zh: 問「你好嗎」很安全，問「你是做什麼的」很安全，但如果你想讓人記住你、想真正點燃連結，那些問題幫不了你。

lines.en: so it does take a little bit of courage to ask this but the answers you're going to get are incredibly interesting you're going to get stories you're going to a hint at values.
lines.zh: 所以問這個確實需要一點勇氣，但你得到的答案會非常有趣，你會聽到故事，會隱約看到對方的價值觀。

lines.en: If you want to know if they're married or have kids, they probably will tell you by accident.
lines.zh: 如果你想知道他們有沒有結婚、有沒有小孩，他們大概會不小心告訴你。

lines.en: So, it's like a hunt for stories.
lines.zh: 所以這就像是在尋找故事。

lines.en: Same with, right, I mentioned this one in the study.
lines.zh: 還有這個，對，我在研究裡提過的。

lines.en: So, working on anything exciting these days.
lines.zh: 「最近有在忙什麼令人興奮的事嗎？」

lines.en: This is again one of my favorite swap questions cuz you're hunting for something good.
lines.zh: 這也是我最喜歡的替換問題之一，因為你在尋找好的東西。

lines.en: Now, when I think about conversation in level one, you're trying to gift someone a chemical cocktail a little bit.
lines.zh: 當我想到第一層的對話，你某種程度上是在送對方一杯化學雞尾酒。

lines.en: And I think in level one, these two questions are doing a lot of heavy lifting.
lines.zh: 我覺得在第一層，這兩個問題發揮了很大的作用。

lines.en: They are now competing with your feed.
lines.zh: 它們現在是在跟你的動態消息競爭。

lines.en: I went uh to a PTA meeting recently and those are torture if you've ever been to one for any parents. PTA meeting.
lines.zh: 我最近去參加了家長會，如果你是家長、參加過的話，那真的是折磨。家長會。

lines.en: Oh, a parent teacher meeting. Okay. Right.
lines.zh: 喔，家長教師會。好。對。

lines.en: So, a bunch of other parents in the room and I wanted to go meet other moms cuz I just moved across the country to try to meet more people.
lines.zh: 所以房間裡有一堆其他家長，我想去認識其他媽媽，因為我剛搬到國家的另一頭，想多認識一些人。

lines.en: And I was like excited.
lines.zh: 我很興奮。

lines.en: I was like, "Okay, I'm going to meet more moms. Here we go."
lines.zh: 我想：「好，我要去認識更多媽媽了。開始吧。」

lines.en: And I walk in the room and everyone's scrolling. Everyone's on their feed.
lines.zh: 結果我走進房間，每個人都在滑手機。每個人都在看動態消息。

lines.en: And I realized, wow, conversation now. not is not just about a way for me to make friends.
lines.zh: 我才發現，哇，現在的對話不只是我交朋友的方式。

lines.en: It actually has to compete with that feed. Mhm.
lines.zh: 它其實得跟那些動態消息競爭。嗯。

lines.en: I have to make my questions and my answers so dopamine worthy that they're actually going to beat that feed.
lines.zh: 我得讓我的問題和回答有足夠的多巴胺吸引力，才能真正贏過那些動態消息。

lines.en: Otherwise, they're going to go right back to their phone.
lines.zh: 不然他們就會馬上回去看手機。

lines.en: That is why these have to do more lifting.
lines.zh: 這就是為什麼這些問題得發揮更大的作用。

lines.en: Because if I want to compete with the feed, I have to produce dopamine, a little bit of excitement, a little bit of motivation.
lines.zh: 因為如果我想跟動態消息競爭，我就得產生多巴胺，一點點興奮、一點點動力。

lines.en: I also have to create what I would call, forgive me for this word, but conversational confetti.
lines.zh: 我還得創造，請原諒我用這個詞，我稱之為「對話彩帶」的東西。

lines.en: This is like we got to we got to lift a little bit more in our conversations because otherwise someone's going to go right back to scrolling.
lines.zh: 就是我們在對話中得多出一點力，不然對方就會馬上回去滑手機。

lines.en: Their brain is somewhere else.
lines.zh: 他們的大腦在別的地方。

lines.en: Either their brain is in their email list or their brain is on their feed.
lines.zh: 不是在想他們的 email 清單，就是在想他們的動態消息。

lines.en: In this research when I was studying amazing conversationalists, one of the one people I studied is Howard Stern.
lines.zh: 在這項研究中，我研究很棒的對話高手，我研究的其中一個人是 Howard Stern。

lines.en: So, however you feel about Howard Stern, he is a master conversationalist.
lines.zh: 不管你對 Howard Stern 有什麼看法，他都是個對話高手。

lines.en: I mean, he can carry on long very interesting.
lines.zh: 我是說，他可以聊很久，非常有趣。

lines.en: He gets people to say things that I could never imagine.
lines.zh: 他能讓人說出我根本想像不到的事。

lines.en: So, I analyzed thousands of transcripts of his interviews and I found one pattern.
lines.zh: 所以我分析了他幾千份訪談逐字稿，發現了一個模式。

lines.en: He does a very good job of creating information gaps.
lines.zh: 他非常擅長製造資訊缺口。

lines.en: So, he'll say, "What's the weirdest thing you've ever done?"
lines.zh: 他會說：「你做過最奇怪的事是什麼？」

lines.en: Or he'll say, "The most surprising thing I heard that happened to me yesterday.
lines.zh: 或是他會說：「我聽說昨天發生在我身上最令人驚訝的一件事，

lines.en: You want to hear what it was?"
lines.zh: 你想聽是什麼嗎？」

lines.en: And your brain doesn't like not knowing.
lines.zh: 而你的大腦不喜歡不知道。

lines.en: So, when it hears the most surprising, the weirdest, the biggest, the worst, the most embarrassing, the brain creates this gap. like this is information gap where the brain is like I have to know
lines.zh: 所以當它聽到「最令人驚訝」「最奇怪」「最大」「最糟」「最丟臉」，大腦就會產生這個缺口，這就是資訊缺口，大腦會想：我一定要知道

lines.en: what is the weirdest thing.
lines.zh: 最奇怪的事是什麼。

lines.en: So also what happens with these kinds of questions is we're creating these little information gaps and actually saying and using in conversation these phrases is a way that we can create more intrigue and interest.
lines.zh: 所以這類問題的另一個作用，是我們在製造這些小小的資訊缺口，而在對話中說出、使用這些詞，是一種能製造更多好奇和興趣的方法。

lines.en: And I I know that sounds like what? But think about this.
lines.zh: 我知道這聽起來很奇怪，但想想看。

lines.en: If something crazy happened to you yesterday and you walk into dinner and you're like guys the craziest thing happened to me yesterday. Everyone's like phone's down.
lines.zh: 如果你昨天發生了一件很瘋狂的事，你走進晚餐聚會說：「各位，我昨天發生了最瘋狂的事。」每個人都會放下手機。

lines.en: Mhm. Right now, I couldn't say something boring.
lines.zh: 嗯。這時我就不能說很無聊的事。

lines.en: I couldn't be like, I was stuck in traffic unless you want to be funny.
lines.zh: 我不能說：我塞在車陣裡，除非你想搞笑。

lines.en: But I think that looking for opportunities to create that little bit of conversational confetti, they come up with questions like this.
lines.zh: 但我覺得去找機會創造那一點點對話彩帶，就會想出這樣的問題。

lines.en: This is the last one.
lines.zh: 這是最後一個。

lines.en: So, have any fun plans coming up?
lines.zh: 「最近有什麼好玩的計畫嗎？」

lines.en: Now, the reason why this one is important, and I agonized over this, over this third question, cuz there's three questions for each level, is have any fun plans coming up, is a subtle way to bring up potential shared future.
lines.zh: 這個問題之所以重要，我為這第三個問題苦思了很久，因為每一層都有三個問題，「最近有什麼好玩的計畫嗎？」是一種巧妙帶出潛在共同未來的方法。

lines.en: Psychologically speaking, we bond with someone when we feel like we could do something fun with them or they're doing something fun that I would also like to do.
lines.zh: 從心理學來說，當我們覺得可以和某人一起做好玩的事，或他們在做一件我也想做的好玩的事，我們就會和對方建立連結。

lines.en: I think that part of these questions is being known for asking better questions like being known for searching for hunt or hunting for excitement
lines.zh: 我覺得這些問題的其中一部分，是讓自己以問出更好的問題出名，以尋找令人興奮的事出名，

lines.en: because what will happen is with people who know you at work or your work friends or uh outside of work friends is they'll bring these things to you.
lines.zh: 因為接下來會發生的是，職場上認識你的人、你的同事朋友或工作以外的朋友，會主動把這些事帶來跟你分享。

lines.en: They know that you're going to ask out personal passions.
lines.zh: 他們知道你會問他們個人熱衷的事。

lines.en: So next time you get to say, "Hey, last time we were talking you mentioned XYZ. How's that going?"
lines.zh: 所以下次你就可以說：「嘿，上次聊天時你提到某某事，進行得怎麼樣？」

lines.en: So they also become your call backs.
lines.zh: 所以它們也會成為你可以回頭提起的話題。

lines.en: They make conversation easier later.
lines.zh: 它們會讓之後的對話更容易。

lines.en: Everybody's starting from a remarkably different place here, aren't they?
lines.zh: 每個人在這方面的起點都非常不一樣，對吧？

lines.en: In in terms of both skill, but also like will
lines.zh: 不管是技巧，還是意願，

lines.en: and energy and like willing to do it. Energy.
lines.zh: 還有能量，還有願不願意去做。能量。

lines.en: Like I think there'll be a lot of uh one might say introverts listening right now that just think what's the point? Like
lines.zh: 我覺得現在可能有很多人，可以說是內向的人，正在聽，然後想：這有什麼意義？

lines.en: you know I don't like people anyway and it's so much energy and I've got to ask these questions and pretend to be interested.
lines.zh: 你知道，我本來就不喜歡人，這很耗能量，我還得問這些問題、假裝有興趣。

lines.en: This is going to drain me. Oh my gosh. I I agree.
lines.zh: 這會把我榨乾。天啊。我同意。

lines.en: And two things can be true.
lines.zh: 兩件事可以同時成立。

lines.en: It's very exhausting in the sense of you're trying, right?
lines.zh: 從你很努力這個角度來說，確實很累，對吧？

lines.en: Like we're putting energy into conversation, but it's also exhausting to have really shallow small talk.

lines.en: So, this is us going deeper with the person. Exactly.
lines.zh: 所以這是我們和對方更深入的時候。沒錯。

lines.en: Or or leveling up as you wish. Right. As you wish.
lines.zh: 或是隨你喜歡說「升級」。對。隨你喜歡。

lines.en: So, the mistake traps people make is they skip level one.
lines.zh: 所以人們常犯的錯，是跳過第一層。

lines.en: They try to go too deep too quickly and people feel like it's invasive. Right?
lines.zh: 他們試著太快太深入，對方會覺得被侵犯，對吧？

lines.en: Especially when you're like, "Whoa, slow down."
lines.zh: 尤其是當你會想：「哇，慢一點。」

lines.en: Or it can feel like an interrogation.
lines.zh: 或者會感覺像在被審問。

lines.en: So, we must know those basics first, as long as we do them better.
lines.zh: 所以我們必須先知道那些基本資訊，只要我們做得更好就好。

lines.en: Like, we don't do them in autopilot way.
lines.zh: 就是不要用自動駕駛的方式做。

lines.en: Level two is when you start to understand what motivates someone.
lines.zh: 第二層是你開始了解什麼能激勵一個人的時候。

lines.en: The kind of mental trick that I use is, you know, you're on level two with someone if you know what gets them up in the morning, like what goal is driving them all day, but you also know what keeps them up at night,
lines.zh: 我用的一個思考小技巧是，你知道，如果你知道什麼讓對方早上起床，也就是什麼目標驅動他一整天，同時也知道什麼讓他晚上睡不著，

lines.en: what worries them.
lines.zh: 什麼讓他煩惱，那你和對方就在第二層了。

lines.en: I, you know, I I encourage people as they're reading like think of the five people you interact with most and place them on a level.
lines.zh: 我鼓勵大家在讀的時候，想想你最常互動的五個人，把他們放到某一層。

lines.en: Like, do you only know the basic facts about them?
lines.zh: 像是，你只知道他們的基本資訊嗎？

lines.en: Are you all the way at level three, which we're going to get to? It's sometimes helpful. You'll notice patterns.
lines.zh: 還是你已經到了第三層，這個我們等一下會談到？這有時很有幫助，你會發現一些模式。

lines.en: Like, I don't know about you, but I love level two.
lines.zh: 像是，我不知道你怎麼樣，但我很愛第二層。

lines.en: Like, I want to get through level one as quickly as possible.
lines.zh: 我想盡快通過第一層。

lines.en: I I want to get to your motivations.
lines.zh: 我想知道你的動機。

lines.en: I want to get to your secret side hustle.
lines.zh: 我想知道你的秘密副業。

lines.en: I want to get to your dreams and passions.
lines.zh: 我想知道你的夢想和熱情。

lines.en: I want to know what keeps you up at night, but I can sometimes jump too fast. Mhm.
lines.zh: 我想知道什麼讓你晚上睡不著，但我有時會跳得太快。嗯。

lines.en: Level two is about making someone feel heard and understood.
lines.zh: 第二層的重點是讓對方覺得被傾聽、被理解。

lines.en: And this is different than discovering treasure.
lines.zh: 這和發掘寶藏不一樣。

lines.en: And the biggest skill that we can do in level two is what I call dream building.
lines.zh: 而在第二層我們能發揮的最大技巧，我稱之為「築夢」。

lines.en: So dream building is everyone has like a secret desire, a secret dream, a secret side hustle, a secret passion.
lines.zh: 築夢就是，每個人都有一個秘密的渴望、秘密的夢想、秘密的副業、秘密的熱情。

lines.en: Can you be there and help them uncover it?
lines.zh: 你能不能在那裡幫他們把它挖掘出來？

lines.en: That's the goal of level two.
lines.zh: 這就是第二層的目標。

lines.en: So give me an example of dream building. Okay.
lines.zh: 給我一個築夢的例子。好。

lines.en: So before we started, I said to you, I have I have a new goal, right?
lines.zh: 在我們開始之前，我跟你說我有一個新目標，對吧？

lines.en: Like I'm I'm pitching a TV show.
lines.zh: 我在提案一個電視節目。

lines.en: That's like my secret side hustle.
lines.zh: 那就像是我的秘密副業。

lines.en: That's level two for me.
lines.zh: 那對我來說就是第二層。

lines.en: It's something that I've been working on secretly and quietly.
lines.zh: 那是我一直在秘密、低調進行的事。

lines.en: And if we were at lunch, we would have I would have told you all about it.
lines.zh: 如果我們在吃午餐，我會把一切都告訴你。

lines.en: We double clicked on it.
lines.zh: 我們會深入聊這件事。

lines.en: So like that's an example of one.
lines.zh: 所以這就是一個例子。

lines.en: Another example to think about is what does someone daydream about, right?
lines.zh: 另一個可以思考的例子是：對方會做什麼白日夢，對吧？

lines.en: Like what is what is occupying their mind in a good way?
lines.zh: 什麼事以好的方式佔據了他們的心思？

lines.en: The other way that I a framework that I give for folks uh is a pet or pest project.
lines.zh: 我給大家的另一個架構是「寵物專案」和「害蟲專案」。

lines.en: So, what is someone's pet project?
lines.zh: 所以，一個人的寵物專案是什麼？

lines.en: Like a pet at home, you kind of think about it, you dream about it, you hope about it.
lines.zh: 就像家裡的寵物，你會想著它、夢想著它、對它懷抱希望。

lines.en: Like, what is someone hoping to achieve or find or do?
lines.zh: 像是，一個人希望達成、找到或做到什麼？

lines.en: And what is their pest project?
lines.zh: 那他們的害蟲專案是什麼？

lines.en: Like, a pest in the attic. It worries you.
lines.zh: 就像閣樓裡的害蟲，它讓你煩惱。

lines.en: You wonder like, how can I get rid of that pest?
lines.zh: 你會想：我要怎麼擺脫那隻害蟲？

lines.en: How can I um eradicate it?
lines.zh: 我要怎麼，嗯，根除它？

lines.en: And they want help with it, but they're too afraid to ask.
lines.zh: 他們想要人幫忙，但又不敢開口。

lines.en: Pest projects have a lot of shame.
lines.zh: 害蟲專案常伴隨著很多羞愧感。

lines.en: On level two, people have to feel safe enough to expose what they feel shame about.
lines.zh: 在第二層，人們必須感到足夠安全，才會揭露讓他們羞愧的事。

lines.en: But pet projects, the things they love, have a lot of pride.
lines.zh: 但寵物專案，也就是他們熱愛的事，則帶著很多驕傲。

lines.en: And so you're trying to figure out in conversation, could you let someone feel safe enough to share either one?
lines.zh: 所以你在對話中試著弄清楚：你能不能讓對方感到足夠安全，分享其中任何一種？

lines.en: And are there questions that evoke dream building? Yes. Okay.
lines.zh: 有沒有能引發築夢的問題？有。好。

lines.en: So what have you always wanted to learn is an interesting question because it it triggers growth mindset, right?
lines.zh: 「你一直想學什麼？」是一個有意思的問題，因為它會觸發成長型思維，對吧？

lines.en: So growth mindset is when someone believes they can change themselves, change who they are, change their trajectory, learn something new.
lines.zh: 成長型思維就是一個人相信自己可以改變，改變自己是誰、改變自己的人生軌跡、學習新東西。

lines.en: So we we like this question because you're asking, "Are you willing to grow with me?
lines.zh: 我們喜歡這個問題，因為你是在問：「你願意和我一起成長嗎？

lines.en: What have you always wanted to learn?"
lines.zh: 你一直想學什麼？」

lines.en: The other easy one is, "What is your biggest goal right now?"
lines.zh: 另一個簡單的問題是：「你現在最大的目標是什麼？」

lines.en: So what is your biggest goal right now is a great question, and you can also time anchor it.
lines.zh: 「你現在最大的目標是什麼？」是一個很棒的問題，你也可以把它和時間點連結。

lines.en: Anytime someone has a birthday, you can ask, "What's your big goal this year?"
lines.zh: 每當有人過生日，你可以問：「你今年的大目標是什麼？」

lines.en: That's actually a level two question, right? you're like like leveling them up in a safe way because they're talking about their birthday any around New Year's January and December.
lines.zh: 那其實是一個第二層的問題，對吧？你是用安全的方式讓對方升級，因為他們在聊自己的生日，或是在新年前後的一月和十二月。

lines.en: I ask everyone I know what's your biggest goal right now, new quarter, new performance review.
lines.zh: 我會問我認識的每個人：你現在最大的目標是什麼？新的一季、新的績效考核。

lines.en: When we talk about goals, it activates a part of our brain that triggers dopamine.
lines.zh: 當我們談論目標時，會活化大腦中觸發多巴胺的部分。

lines.en: When we think about our future self, it activates a part of ourselves that wants to get motivated.
lines.zh: 當我們想到未來的自己，會活化我們內在想要振作起來的部分。

lines.en: And so level two is also giving someone motivation that in conversation, they're actually discovering an aspect of themselves.
lines.zh: 所以第二層也是在給對方動力，讓他們在對話中其實在發掘自己的某一面。

lines.en: They're tapping into their own resource for motivation.
lines.zh: 他們在汲取自己內在的動力資源。

lines.en: It gives them permission to dream a little bit and to Yeah.
lines.zh: 這允許他們稍微做點夢，然後……對。

lines.en: And you're giving them the motivation that they already have, but you're bringing it into the conversation.
lines.zh: 你是在給他們本來就有的動力，但你把它帶進了對話裡。

lines.en: I think recently we are so into intrapersonal.
lines.zh: 我覺得最近我們太專注在自我內在了。

lines.en: Like a lot of what you see on social media right now is mindset and mantra and affirmation and productivity.
lines.zh: 你現在在社群媒體上看到的很多東西，都是心態、口號、肯定語和生產力。

lines.en: And I love all of those things.
lines.zh: 我很喜歡這些東西。

lines.en: But that means that people are actually using all that excitement alone when they're journaling or when they're meditating or when they're working on their to-do list.
lines.zh: 但這代表大家其實是在獨自寫日記、冥想或處理待辦清單時，自己一個人消化那些興奮感。

lines.en: We have forgotten, I've noticed, to bring those goals into conversation. We're almost like embarrassed.
lines.zh: 我注意到，我們忘了把這些目標帶進對話裡。我們幾乎覺得很不好意思。

lines.en: I don't know if you've noticed this, but I've it's almost like people are like embarrassed to talk about their secret side hustle or they're embarrassed to talk about their secret passion.
lines.zh: 我不知道你有沒有注意到，但大家幾乎都不好意思談自己的秘密副業，或是不好意思談自己秘密的熱情。

lines.en: If we give someone permission to bring in what they have been motivated about privately into conversation, they get you get to be an ally. with a dead end when you ask these kind of level two questions.
lines.zh: 如果我們允許對方把私下讓他們有動力的事帶進對話，他們就……你就能成為他們的盟友。如果你問這類第二層問題時碰到死胡同呢？

lines.en: Well, then you get to answer
lines.zh: 那你就可以回答，

lines.en: because some people haven't quite figured out what their biggest goal is. Absolutely.
lines.zh: 因為有些人還沒完全想清楚自己最大的目標是什麼。沒錯。

lines.en: Especially also sometimes um introverts in conversation and I've asked these questions to thousands of people and all different kinds of things happen when I do that.
lines.zh: 尤其有時候內向的人在對話中……我問過幾千個人這些問題，每次都會發生各種不同的狀況。

lines.en: Introverts also need more time to process.
lines.zh: 內向的人也需要更多時間消化。

lines.en: So you might ask them, you know, what are you learning right now or what's your biggest goal?
lines.zh: 所以你可能問他們：你現在在學什麼？或你最大的目標是什麼？

lines.en: And they might in the moment not know.
lines.zh: 他們當下可能不知道。

lines.en: They just need a little bit of time to process.
lines.zh: 他們只是需要一點時間消化。

lines.en: And so two things can happen is if they don't have it yet, that's okay.
lines.zh: 所以可能發生兩件事：如果他們還沒有答案，那也沒關係。

lines.en: You also have opportunity to share.
lines.zh: 你也有機會分享。

lines.en: But what if I, you know, I ask, I'm thinking because, you know, I know a lot of uh taxi drivers listen to this podcast cuz I get in taxis and we talk about it.
lines.zh: 但如果我……你知道，我在想，因為我知道很多計程車司機會聽這個 podcast，因為我搭計程車時會跟他們聊到。

lines.en: Taxi drivers, you know, they're conversationalists, often very good ones.
lines.zh: 計程車司機，你知道，他們都很會聊天，常常非常會聊。

lines.en: Um, but sometimes I guess a taxi driver might be faced with the scenario where the person in the back seat doesn't want to talk and they might hit them with one of these,
lines.zh: 嗯，但有時候我猜計程車司機可能會遇到後座乘客不想聊天的情況，他們可能丟出其中一個

lines.en: you know, level ones and then the level twos and and they're just getting brick walls.
lines.zh: 第一層的問題，然後是第二層的問題，結果一直碰壁。

lines.en: Then I would respect that, right?
lines.zh: 那我會尊重這一點，對吧？

lines.en: If someone doesn't want to talk to you,
lines.zh: 如果有人不想跟你聊，

lines.en: do you just back out? Yeah. Okay.
lines.zh: 你就退出嗎？對。好。

lines.en: Because then they're going through their own thing, right?
lines.zh: 因為他們正在經歷自己的事，對吧？

lines.en: Like if if you have to have also courage to be disliked, right?
lines.zh: 就像你也得有被討厭的勇氣，對吧？

lines.en: Like you can try your best in conversation.
lines.zh: 你可以在對話中盡力而為。

lines.en: You can bring the best questions, but if someone is not your person or they are not ready to connect, why would you waste your energy on that?
lines.zh: 你可以拿出最好的問題，但如果對方不是你的人，或是他們還沒準備好建立連結，你幹嘛把能量浪費在那上面？

lines.en: So, I also think that asking some of these are like bids.
lines.zh: 所以我也覺得問這些問題就像是在「出價」。

lines.en: It's like a bid to see like, can we can we do this?
lines.zh: 就像是出個價，看看：我們可以這樣聊嗎？

lines.en: You want to banter with me?
lines.zh: 你想跟我打趣嗎？

lines.en: Should we have level one?
lines.zh: 我們要來聊第一層嗎？

lines.en: Should we even dip into level two? Great. If not, cool. They're not your person. It's not their day.
lines.zh: 我們要不要稍微進到第二層？很好。如果不要，也沒關係。他們不是你的人。今天不是他們的日子。

lines.en: So, if they don't take the bait, it's okay. Okay.
lines.zh: 所以如果他們不上鉤，也沒關係。好。

lines.en: I The taxi drivers usually ask me, um, got anything exciting today?
lines.zh: 計程車司機通常會問我：嗯，今天有什麼令人興奮的事嗎？

lines.en: Are we going anywhere exciting? Great.
lines.zh: 我們要去什麼好玩的地方嗎？很好。

lines.en: That's a great swap for level one.
lines.zh: 那是第一層很棒的替換問題。

lines.en: I should say by the way these questions are suggestions.
lines.zh: 順帶一提，我要說這些問題只是建議。

lines.en: If you can modify them to the to fit what you are doing even better.
lines.zh: 如果你能修改它們，讓它們更符合你在做的事，那就更好了。

lines.en: Like for example, you and I are in book signings or we we are meeting after speaking events.
lines.zh: 例如，你和我會參加簽書會，或在演講後和大家見面。

lines.en: It makes sense for us to modify the learning or goal question to say hey you know what did you learn or did you learn anything new or what was your favorite part?
lines.zh: 對我們來說，把學習或目標的問題改成「嘿，你學到了什麼？」「你有學到什麼新東西嗎？」或「你最喜歡哪個部分？」就很合理。

lines.en: Right? We're modifying that for us.
lines.zh: 對吧？我們是為自己修改。

lines.en: A taxi driver is going to modify it for are we heading anywhere exciting doing anything exciting today?
lines.zh: 計程車司機會把它改成「我們要去什麼好玩的地方嗎？今天有做什麼好玩的事嗎？」

lines.en: So like these are not prescriptions right?
lines.zh: 所以這些不是處方，對吧？

lines.en: They are guidelines to try to make the research applicable.
lines.zh: 它們是指引，讓研究能實際應用。

lines.en: You know, I've spent most of my career looking at research, reading academic studies, and some of them are 30 pages of jargon with one nugget.
lines.zh: 你知道，我職業生涯大部分時間都在看研究、讀學術論文，有些是 30 頁的術語，只有一個重點。

lines.en: And Dan McAdams research is so incredible, but when I first read it, I did not know how to use it.
lines.zh: Dan McAdams 的研究非常了不起，但我第一次讀的時候，不知道要怎麼用。

lines.en: I was like, general traits, personal concerns, like level one. I wasn't sure.
lines.zh: 我想：一般特質、個人關注，像第一層那樣。我不太確定。

lines.en: So, a lot of these are just ways to activate the behavioral research, the guideline that's driving all of our interactions, but you get to have flexibility with it as it works for you.
lines.zh: 所以這些很多只是啟動行為研究的方法，也就是驅動我們所有互動的指引，但你可以依照適合你的方式彈性運用。

lines.en: The goal in level one, treasure hunt. Put someone at ease.
lines.zh: 第一層的目標：尋寶。讓對方放鬆。

lines.en: Ask them about what they love. Harvest story.
lines.zh: 問他們熱愛什麼。收集故事。

lines.en: The goal of level two is to give someone permission to share a dream, a secret desire, or a secret worry.
lines.zh: 第二層的目標是允許對方分享一個夢想、一個秘密的渴望，或一個秘密的煩惱。

lines.en: And level three we get to get to in a little bit when you're ready.
lines.zh: 第三層等你準備好，我們稍後再談。

lines.en: Oh, we have one more level. Level three. Hold on. Level two question on these questions.
lines.zh: 喔，我們還有一層。第三層。等一下。關於這些第二層的問題，

lines.en: Do you have to actually care about the answer?
lines.zh: 你必須真的在乎答案嗎？

lines.en: Do you have to authentically care about what their biggest goal is right now or what their personal passion project is?
lines.zh: 你必須真心在乎對方現在最大的目標是什麼，或他個人熱衷的專案是什麼嗎？

lines.en: Does it matter if you don't actually care?
lines.zh: 如果你其實不在乎，有關係嗎？

lines.en: There have been times in conversation where I'm not sure if I care yet.
lines.zh: 在對話中，有些時候我不確定自己是不是已經在乎了。

lines.en: So, I would say you don't care yet.
lines.zh: 所以我會說，你只是還不在乎。

lines.en: What if you ask the question and you're not sure, you're not bought in yet, but then you hear an answer that deeply resonates with you or you deeply care about.
lines.zh: 如果你問了問題，你不確定、還沒投入，但接著你聽到一個讓你深有共鳴、或你非常在乎的答案呢？

lines.en: I think we don't know always if we're going to care about someone cuz we've just met them.
lines.zh: 我覺得我們不一定知道自己會不會在乎一個人，因為我們才剛認識他們。

lines.en: But maybe you will, right?
lines.zh: 但也許你會，對吧？

lines.en: Like, you never know who's going to be your next best friend, right?
lines.zh: 你永遠不知道誰會成為你下一個最好的朋友，對吧？

lines.en: You never know when when you're going to hear an aha moment that's going to change your business.
lines.zh: 你永遠不知道什麼時候會聽到一個改變你事業的頓悟時刻。

lines.en: Like so many of the pivot points in my business have been from random conversations where I happen to ask the right question and someone gives me a brilliant piece of advice.
lines.zh: 我事業上很多轉折點，都來自一些隨機的對話，我剛好問了對的問題，對方就給了我一個絕妙的建議。

lines.en: So is it okay to pretend to care?
lines.zh: 所以假裝在乎可以嗎？

lines.en: If you're asking the question, you care enough to try. Right?
lines.zh: 如果你問了這個問題，你就已經在乎到願意嘗試了，對吧？
